Enable owner route only after API/security/browser tests and approved configuration; B2B client-company access stays a separate future workstream.

tasks.title: Assess authorised provider and isolated VMMS hosting fit
acceptance: Inspect only necessary provider metadata/configuration with secrets redacted. Record database engine, runtime limits, TLS/pooling, private storage, region and account ownership.
Compare the Fastify/worker/PostgreSQL design with available Vercel/database capabilities and prepare an isolated database/namespace/credential plan preserving the existing portal.
Prepare reviewable staging/production changes, costs, recovery and Cloudflare DNS/TLS entries before external action.

tasks.title: Review hosting assessment and secret isolation
acceptance: Verify provider claims from inspected metadata, no secrets in artifacts, and isolated runtime/migration credentials.
External settings remain proposed until exact authorised changes are performed and verified.

tasks.title: Review launch entry and identity assets
acceptance: Use the public heading Sign in to VMMS, with staff and approved vehicle-owner access in launch scope; keep marketing on the company website.
Use existing logo, icon and browser-tab assets from the Raymond Gray main project; record source/copied paths, hashes and transformations and verify light/dark and tab rendering.
Expose no customer names, VINs, registrations, work counts or searches before authentication. No public self-registration. Only confirmed official-site and support links appear.
The server determines authorised workspaces; enable the owner route only after its authentication, relationship, API and browser checks pass.

tasks.title: Review approved owner launch acceptance
acceptance: Include invited or explicitly approved vehicle owners in launch alongside staff. Later B2B client-company access is separate.

Authorised staff approve time-bounded owner-account/vehicle relationships with evidence. Invitations are identity-bound, expiring and single-use. Shared email/phone, registration or VIN knowledge never grants access.
Owners see only curated customer-facing status, estimates/consent, invoices and handover documents permitted by the originating workflow and their approved relationship.
Enforce tenant/site, ownership interval and document visibility on every API/list/download; exclude internal notes, warranty payer disputes, employee records and previous-owner personal data.
Approval, revocation and ownership transfer are attributable versioned commands. Recheck relationships for every request/download and clear private caches on access loss.

Prove cross-owner and owner-to-staff denial, guessed identifiers, invite replay/expiry, unauthorised approval, transfer/revocation, shared-device sign-out and protected downloads through real API/database and browser checks.
No public signup or VIN/work-order guessing. Owner access grants no staff, technical, release or financial authority. Any enabled consent action binds to its exact approved proposal revision.

tasks.title: Persist reception drafts and scoped queue
acceptance: Create/reload canonical customer/vehicle-linked drafts with server-owned site/tenant and unique visit/work-order IDs.
Queue shows persisted data, loading/empty/failure/stale-version states. No G1 or repair approval is implied.
tasks.statusNote: Scoped reception queue and persisted intake projection are implemented with explicit loading, failure and empty states; browser/API acceptance of all queue states remains in S-004/S-005.

tasks.title: Add C02 and planned tasks to one draft work order
acceptance: Persist C01/C02 complaints and planned tasks on one controlling work order with customer wording and unique ordinals.
Use version/idempotency checks; diagnosis and repair approval remain pending.
tasks.statusNote: C01/C02 and planned task commands use the same versioned, idempotent work order. PostgreSQL/API and authenticated browser evidence cover C02/task persistence and keep tasks planned; broader diagnosis/authorization scope remains outside this slice.

tasks.title: Open protective holds with attributable history
acceptance: Record hold type/severity, owner/source/reason/scope/timestamps without a settled payer.
Commit hold/version/audit/receipt/outbox atomically; show blocked and permitted work without offering release.
tasks.statusNote: Protective hold command records scope, severity, reason/source and actor in the versioned event flow; PostgreSQL and browser evidence prove task scoping. Broader hold lifecycle controls remain future work.

tasks.title: Verify first-slice API persistence and isolation
acceptance: Test drafts, complaints/tasks and holds using PostgreSQL and real runtime role.
Prove site/tenant denial, stale/conflicting replay, rollback and atomic state/audit/receipt/outbox.
tasks.statusNote: The PostgreSQL suite passes with the non-owner runtime role and proves intake, C02, task and hold commands; cross-site/tenant denial; replay/stale-version handling; rollback; and event/receipt/outbox invariants. Tracker verification remains in progress while S-002, S-003 and foundation dependency F-009 are not yet fully verified.

tasks.title: Verify first-slice browser workflow and drafts
acceptance: Use actual browser/API to create draft, add C02/task, open hold, reload and observe history.
Check mobile/keyboard, empty/failure/conflict, draft recovery, sign-out/account switch and offline final-action denial.
tasks.statusNote: Authenticated browser workflow verifies intake, C02, planned task, scoped hold, reload recovery, offline write denial, responsive work-order layouts, keyboard, reduced-motion and sign-out. Browser empty/error/conflict and account/site-switch scenarios remain open.

tasks.title: Accept the bounded first engineering slice
acceptance: Review real API/database/browser evidence and remaining defects for the draft workflow.
This slice does not complete full AT-02 diagnosis, G1-G5, customer launch access or production approval.

tasks.title: Verify launch readiness for staff and approved vehicle owners
acceptance: Every required launch task has reviewed acceptance evidence; every launch requirement is verified or has an explicit valid owner-approved applicability decision. In-progress, planned, deferred or configuration-required work cannot pass this gate.

Confirm approved safety/equipment/authority/finance/privacy/identity settings, staff UAT, owner-access API/browser isolation, saved drafts, private evidence, restore and representative supported-browser results.

Google primary sign-in, passkeys and local email/username-password fallback pass approved-account access tests. Responsive art direction passes asset budgets, width/orientation/zoom, keyboard and touch checks.
Record later real historical import/AT-01, native/platform work and post-pilot Issue 1.0 review explicitly. Their deferral does not waive full-goal completion.
The concrete release/configuration is reviewable and still requires O-019 named pilot approval and authorisation of actual deployment changes.

tasks.title: Define canonical accounts and approved audience access
acceptance: Model canonical account, Google issuer/subject identity, local identifier/credential, passkey credentials and sessions separately from staff membership and owner relationships.
Specify invitation/recovery/linking collision behavior. Normalised shared contact details cannot merge accounts or grant access; staff and owner contexts stay explicit.

tasks.title: Use shared identity provider for email-or-username/password fallback
acceptance: Authenticate through the central identity provider; VMMS never receives, hashes or stores the submitted password.
After provider sign-in, map the stable issuer/subject to a VMMS identity and enforce approved status and allowed audience on the server.
No credential endpoint creates privileges or public registration; pending, suspended and unmapped users are denied.

tasks.title: Use Google sign-in through the central OIDC broker
acceptance: Configure Google identity brokering in the shared provider and use its OIDC authorization-code flow with exact registered callbacks.
Unknown identities and same-email collisions do not auto-provision, merge accounts or create VMMS access.
VMMS receives a validated central issuer/subject and derives current staff/owner permissions from its own records.

tasks.title: Use central passkeys with user verification required
acceptance: Register and authenticate passkeys through the shared identity provider; VMMS does not implement a custom WebAuthn challenge-to-login-token protocol.
Configure the central provider with exact auth origin/RP ID, required user verification and reviewed synced-passkey counter behavior.
Prove provider-side authenticator revocation and affected VMMS session revocation. Passkey possession grants no business access.

tasks.title: Build the VMMS entry and central sign-in experience
acceptance: Keep the current approved Workshop desk visual baseline. VMMS links to the central sign-in service; the central page offers Google, passkey and password methods only when configured.
Provide accessible loading, cancellation, failure and pending-access states without fake enabled controls or account-existence disclosure.
Keep sign-in neutral and route only to server-approved staff or owner workspaces.

tasks.title: Use explicit identity linking and protected account recovery
acceptance: Use the central provider linking/recovery process with recent authentication or the approved independent recovery path.
Reject email-collision takeover, expired/replayed recovery tokens and unauthorised linking; audit lifecycle and revoke sessions as policy requires.
Recovery cannot create staff grants, owner relationships or restore revoked business access.

tasks.title: Verify OIDC integration and application access security
acceptance: Reject wrong issuer/audience/signature, expired tokens, replayed state/code, bad nonce, PKCE mismatch and redirect mismatch.
Test provider account-linking and recovery denial paths, local session expiry/revocation and audit trails.
Prove no authentication path creates or restores VMMS business permission.

tasks.title: Exercise browser OIDC login and virtual passkeys
acceptance: Use local Keycloak and virtual authenticators for registration/login, required user verification, revocation and recovery denial paths.
Exercise provider Google fixtures, central password fallback, approved staff/owner accounts, workspace selection, session expiry, shared-device sign-out and keyboard/touch/error states.
Separate virtual provider and authenticator results from actual Google and physical device evidence.

tasks.title: Configure the shared auth origin, Google callbacks and passkey RP
acceptance: Record exact staging/production Google callbacks and secret owners without secret values.
Set passkey RP ID/origin to the auth service origin, not the VMMS relying-party origin; staging and production use distinct approved environments.
Verify exact provider/domain changes and staging success/denial behavior. Proposed production settings are not deployed claims.

tasks.title: Accept central authentication across VMMS launch audiences
acceptance: Exercise Google, central passkey and password fallback through the configured staging identity service using approved staff/owner accounts.
Confirm each mapped identity still needs the VMMS-approved audience and current resource grants.
Record callback, RP/origin, fallback, recovery/session and supported-device results with reviewer sign-off; unresolved defects remain blocking.

tasks.title: Define responsive compositions and asset delivery budgets
acceptance: Record intended mobile/tablet/foldable/desktop compositions, essential subject safe areas and source-generation/provenance. Logo/essential text must remain readable rather than clipped.
Set reviewable image byte/resolution budgets by viewport, format and above-fold total; measure actual delivered resources and avoid loading all art variants.

tasks.title: Create and inspect art-directed image variants
acceptance: Produce supporting image variants suited to required aspect ratios; inspect each for preserved subject matter and usable composition. Keep approved logo/icon assets faithful and separate.
Record paths, dimensions, formats, byte counts and generation/edit provenance; reject variants with cropped essential subjects, unintended text or excessive delivery weight.

tasks.title: Implement responsive image selection and layouts
acceptance: Use picture/srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions to select appropriate variants and avoid layout shifts; respect reduced motion and accessible decoration/content semantics.
Check image choice at mobile/tablet/fold/desktop widths; no clipped logos/essential subject or unnecessary hidden-image downloads.
Keep sign-in/queue/owner controls usable with wrapping, content expansion and intentional accessible overflow for genuinely wide tables only.

tasks.title: Sweep widths, orientation, zoom and foldable layouts
acceptance: Continuously resize each main workflow across the declared width range and inspect between breakpoints, portrait/landscape and foldable viewport/posture conditions. Record sweep range and any actual-hardware limits.
At 200/400 percent zoom and expanded text, check no clipped labels, unreachable controls, accidental page overflow or inadequate touch targets. Verify keyboard focus and navigation.
Capture failures and evidence for entry, all auth methods, staff queue/detail and owner views across the browser matrix.

tasks.title: Verify delivered image budgets and composition
acceptance: Measure selected image URLs, decoded dimensions, transferred bytes and layout shift on each target viewport/network profile; enforce the approved budgets.
Review light/dark, portrait/landscape/fold/desktop compositions and browser icons for no essential cropping/distortion. Record actual browser screenshots and remaining limitations.

tasks.title: Review launch authentication methods
acceptance: Provide Google SSO as the main sign-in provider, passkeys, and email-or-username/password fallback for both staff and approved vehicle owners. All methods resolve one canonical account with separately approved audience/relationship access.
Successful authentication never creates staff membership, owner relationships or technical/financial authority. No public signup or access-by-email/VIN guessing.

Validate Google issuer/audience/verified subject and the approved invitation/account-linking policy; use OAuth/OIDC state, nonce, PKCE and exact approved callback origins. Never automatically merge identities by matching email alone.

Passkey registration/authentication/revocation/recovery uses short-lived one-use challenges bound to account/session/operation, expected RP ID and origin, credential ownership and required user verification. Verify replay and concurrent challenge use fail.

Normalise supported email/username identifiers consistently, keep passwords securely hashed, rate-limit authentication and recovery, prevent enumeration and enforce session revocation and CSRF controls.

Test all three methods, credential linking/collisions/recovery, expired/revoked sessions and staff/owner isolation through real API/database and browser workflows; use virtual-authenticator tests plus actual-device evidence for declared passkey support.

tasks.title: Review responsive art direction and browser evidence
acceptance: Design generated supporting imagery for mobile, tablet, foldable and desktop aspect ratios. Preserve essential subject matter, text and logos; never rely on accidental cropping of one desktop image.
Use appropriate picture/srcset/sizes sources and formats, measured byte budgets and intrinsic dimensions. Keep original Raymond Gray identity assets separate and faithfully rendered.

Exercise continuous browser resizing, portrait/landscape and foldable widths/postures, text expansion and 200/400 percent zoom. No clipped text, hidden actions, accidental page overflow or unusable touch targets.
Verify public entry, all sign-in methods, staff queues and approved-owner views across the declared browser/device matrix. Publish untested hardware and OS limitations honestly.

tasks.title: Prepare concrete professional visual directions
acceptance: Compare the current baseline with two distinct proposals in a separate reviewable artifact using actual brand assets.

tasks.title: Record owner visual-direction decision
acceptance: Record explicit owner selection, including choosing the current baseline, before applying a new artistic direction.

tasks.title: Verify approved design across layouts
acceptance: Apply only the selected direction and attach desktop, phone, tablet, foldable and zoom evidence with readable brand/form and no clipped essential content.

tasks.title: Run the isolated local shared identity provider
acceptance: Start Keycloak and PostgreSQL from the local-only compose stack with loopback binding and synthetic accounts.
Create a versioned development realm with closed registration and passkey user verification required.
Prove health, restart persistence and clean teardown without any production credentials.
tasks.statusNote: local_passkey_enrollment_and_passwordless_login_passed

tasks.title: Integrate VMMS as the first OIDC relying party
acceptance: VMMS completes server-side OIDC authorization code with state, nonce, exact issuer/audience/callback and PKCE S256 validation.
Browser receives only a VMMS host-only HttpOnly session; provider tokens remain server-side.
Existing per-site and staff/customer grants still decide access on every protected request.
tasks.statusNote: local_provider_passkey_ceremony_passed_production_gaps_open

tasks.title: Move platform sign-in to the shared identity service
acceptance: Platform maps issuer/subject to its existing product-local user and preserves its approved/suspended and role checks.
Remove the custom passkey challenge-to-login-token exchange after OIDC replacement is proven.
Prove unauthorized, pending and suspended platform users remain denied.

tasks.title: Audit and integrate remaining authenticated products
acceptance: Trace actual protected routes and product-local permissions in remote support and vehicle services.
Integrate OIDC only for features that require authentication; keep public intake pages accessible.
Verify product access is isolated and local roles remain authoritative.

tasks.title: Verify shared identity security and revocation
acceptance: Reject wrong issuer/audience/signature, expired tokens, replayed state/code, invalid nonce, PKCE mismatch and redirect mismatch.
Exercise Google linking without email auto-link, passkey user verification, account disablement and local session revocation.
Test app-specific authorization after identity login and logout.

tasks.title: Prove production identity operations and recovery
acceptance: Select a persistent runtime and supported PostgreSQL with monitored health, restricted administration, backup and tested restore.
Rehearse upgrade, outage, account recovery and credential rotation procedures.
Keep production blocked until the concrete host, Google setup, secret store and named operator are reviewed.

tasks.title: Run the per-service Cloudflare and Vercel compatibility review
acceptance: Build a service matrix for VMMS, platform, remote support, vehicle services and shared auth.
Run a synthetic VMMS Workers/Hyperdrive compatibility spike for Fastify, pg, transactions/RLS and uploads.
Check each Next.js framework adapter, Node/native packages, image pipeline, caching, background work and OIDC.
Record cost, region, rollback and provider-specific risks; do not change production DNS.

tasks.title: Review concrete staging hosting and recovery plan
acceptance: Present an exact per-service provider/runtime, database region, domain, secrets, backup and rollback plan.
Prove staging build and critical workflow tests on selected runtimes using synthetic data.
Obtain owner review before creating production provider resources or changing DNS.

tasks.title: Apply restrained semantic color accents in a later design pass
acceptance: Propose a restrained palette with small tags, thin highlights or edge rules; do not use large full-color cards.
Obtain owner review before applying the visual change.
Verify contrast and that statuses remain understandable without color.

tasks.title: Shared identity provider and cross-product sign-in
acceptance: Deliver the standalone identity service and integrate authenticated products through the shared OIDC contract.
Keep app-specific access grants in product-owned records.
